collection.name: Lojban through dialogues
collection.description: Progressive 30-lesson course (Lifri, Mentu, Linto): one level per lesson = info card, phrases, dialogue last; stories 01-05 interleaved. All Lojban validated with egglog-lojban.

items.free_content_front: Lesson 1: First Meeting — lo pa moi nu penmi
items.free_content_back:
#### New words
{coi}, {co'o}, {mi'e}, {la}, {cliva}, {do}

#### Grammar
One word is already a full sentence: `coi` (hello), `co'o` (goodbye). `coi do` greets you; `coi .lifris.` greets Lifri by name. `mi'e la .mentus.` = "I'm Mentu".

items.free_content_front:
# lo pa moi nu penmi
Lifri(F): coi do
~ Hello!
Mentu(M): coi .i mi'e la .mentus.
~ Hi! I'm Mentu.
Lifri(F): mi'e la .lifris.
~ I'm Lifri.
> .i la .lintas. cu klama
~ Linto arrives.
Linto(F): coi .lifris. coi .mentus.
~ Hi Lifri! Hi Mentu!
Lifri(F): coi .lintas.
~ Hi, Linto!
Mentu(M): .i mi cliva .i co'o
~ I'm leaving. Bye!
Linto(F): co'o .mentus.
~ Bye, Mentu!
items.free_content_back:
First Meeting.
Lifri: Hello!
Mentu: Hi! I'm Mentu.
Lifri: I'm Lifri.
Linto arrives.
Linto: Hi Lifri! Hi Mentu!
Lifri: Hi, Linto!
Mentu: I'm leaving. Bye!
Linto: Bye, Mentu!

items.free_content_front: Lesson 2: Do You Speak Lojban? — xu do se bangu la .lojban.
items.free_content_back:
#### New words
{xu}, se bangu, {go'i}, {na}, {milxe}, {mi}

#### Grammar
`xu` turns a sentence into a yes/no question. Answer `go'i` (yes, it's so) or `na go'i` (no). `milxe` softens: `mi milxe se bangu` = I speak a little.

items.free_content_front: xu do se bangu lo glico bangu

# xu do se bangu la .lojban.
Lifri(F): coi .mentus. .i xu do se bangu la .lojban.
~ Hi Mentu! Do you speak Lojban?
Mentu(M): go'i .i mi milxe se bangu la .lojban.
~ Yes. I speak Lojban a little.
Linto(F): .i xu do se bangu lo glico bangu
~ Do you speak English?
Mentu(M): go'i
~ Yes.
Linto(F): .i mi na se bangu lo glico bangu
~ I don't speak English.
Lifri(F): .i ku'i do se bangu la .lojban.
~ But you speak Lojban.
Linto(F): go'i
~ Yes!
items.free_content_back:
Do You Speak Lojban?.
Lifri: Hi Mentu! Do you speak Lojban?
Mentu: Yes. I speak Lojban a little.
Linto: Do you speak English?
Mentu: Yes.
Linto: I don't speak English.
Lifri: But you speak Lojban.
Linto: Yes!

items.free_content_front: Lesson 3: What's Your Name? What Do You Like? — ma cmene do
items.free_content_back:
#### New words
{ma}, {mo}, {cmene}, {zo}, {nelci}

#### Grammar
`ma` asks for a missing noun, `mo` for a missing predicate. `zo` quotes one word: `zo .mentus. cmene mi` = "Mentu" is my name. `do mo` = how are you?

items.free_content_front:
# ma cmene do
Linto(F): coi .i ma cmene do
~ Hi! What's your name?
Mentu(M): zo .mentus. cmene mi .i ma cmene do
~ My name is Mentu. What's your name?
Linto(F): mi'e la .lintas.
~ I'm Linto.
Lifri(F): .i do nelci ma
~ What do you like?
Linto(F): .i mi nelci lo ckafi
~ I like coffee.
Mentu(M): .i mi nelci la .lojban.
~ I like Lojban!
Lifri(F): .ui
~ Great!
items.free_content_back:
What's Your Name? What Do You Like?.
Linto: Hi! What's your name?
Mentu: My name is Mentu. What's your name?
Linto: I'm Linto.
Lifri: What do you like?
Linto: I like coffee.
Mentu: I like Lojban!
Lifri: Great!

items.free_content_front: Lesson 4: Thank You — Wrapping Up the Meetup — ki'e
items.free_content_back:
#### New words
{ki'e}, {je'e}, {.ui}, {.u'u}, {pei}, {.e'u}

#### Grammar
Attitudinals are whole sentences or go before one. `pei` asks how the other person feels: `.ui pei` = are you happy? `.e'u` suggests: `.e'u mi'o ba penmi` = let's meet again.

items.collection_note: doubtful: je'e ("roger") as the answer to ki'e follows common usage; CLL gives no dedicated "you're welcome"

Lifri(F): je'e

Linto(F): .ui .i mi nelci la .lojban.
~ Yay! I like Lojban!
Mentu(M): .u'u doi .lintas.
~ Sorry, Linto!
Linto(F): je'e
~ It's OK.
Lifri(F): .ui .i .ui pei
~ I'm happy! And you?
Mentu(M): .ui
~ Happy!
Linto(F): .e'u mi'o ba penmi
~ Let's meet again!

items.free_content_front: Lesson 5: Let's Meet at the Park — mi klama le panka
items.free_content_back:
#### New words
{zvati}, {klama}, {le}, {zdani}, {panka}

#### Grammar
`le` = the (one I have in mind). `klama`: x1 goes to x2 from x3. `ma nuzba` = what's new?

items.free_content_front:
# mi klama le panka
Lifri(F): coi .mentus. .i ma nuzba
~ Hi Mentu! What's new?
Mentu(M): no da
~ Nothing.
Lifri(F): .i do zvati ma
~ Where are you?
Mentu(M): .i mi zvati le zdani .i do zvati ma
~ I'm at home. Where are you?
Lifri(F): .i mi zvati le panka
~ I'm at the park.
Mentu(M): .ui .i mi klama le panka
~ Great! I'm coming to the park.
Lifri(F): .ui
~ Great!

Let's Meet at the Park.
Lifri: Hi Mentu! What's new?
Mentu: Nothing.
Lifri: Where are you?
Mentu: I'm at home. Where are you?

items.free_content_front: Lesson 6: What Time? Let's Say Seven — ti'u li ze
items.free_content_back:
#### New words
{pa}, {re}, {ci}, {vo}, {mu}, {xa}, {ze}, {bi}, {so}, {no}, {tcika}, {ti'u}, {li}

#### Grammar
Digits chain left to right: `pano` = 10, `reno` = 20. `li` makes a number a noun. `ti'u li xa` = at six o'clock. `ma tcika` = what time is it?

items.free_content_front:
# ti'u li ze
Mentu(M): .i ma tcika
~ What time is it?
Lifri(F): ti'u li xa
~ It's six.
Mentu(M): .i xu mi'o penmi ti'u li ze
~ Shall we meet at seven?
Lifri(F): go'i .i ti'u li ze
~ Yes, at seven.
Mentu(M): .i mi klama le panka ti'u li ze
~ I'm going to the park at seven.
Lifri(F): .ui .i co'o
~ Great! Bye!
items.free_content_back:
What Time? Let's Say Seven.
Mentu: What time is it?
Lifri: It's six.
Mentu: Shall we meet at seven?
Lifri: Yes, at seven.
Mentu: I'm going to the park at seven.
Lifri: Great! Bye!

#### New words
{cerni}, {vanci}, {nicte}, {donri}, {gleki}, {ca}

#### Grammar
`ca le cerni` = in the morning; also `ca le vanci` (evening), `ca le nicte` (night). `cerni coi` / `donri coi` = good morning / good day.

items.free_content_front: Lesson 8: Speak Slowly! I Don't Understand — ko masno tavla
items.free_content_back:
#### New words
{sutra}, {masno}, {ko}, {djuno}, {jimpe}, {preti}

#### Grammar
`ko` makes a command: `ko masno tavla` = speak slowly! `mi na jimpe` = I don't understand; `mi na djuno` = I don't know.

items.free_content_front:
# ko masno tavla
Lifri(F): .i do mo .i ma nuzba .i xu do zvati le panka ca le cerni
~ How are you? What's new? Are you at the park in the mornings?
Mentu(M): .u'u .i mi na jimpe .i ko masno tavla
~ Sorry! I don't understand. Speak slowly!
Linto(F): .i do sutra tavla
~ You speak fast.
Lifri(F): .u'u .i xu do jimpe
~ Sorry. Do you understand now?
Mentu(M): go'i .i mi jimpe .i ki'e
~ Yes, I understand. Thanks!
Linto(F): .i mi ponse pa preti .i ma tcika
~ I have a question. What time is it?
Mentu(M): .i mi na djuno
~ I don't know.
Lifri(F): ti'u li ze
~ Seven o'clock.
items.free_content_back:
Speak Slowly! I Don't Understand.
Lifri: How are you? What's new? Are you at the park in the mornings?
Mentu: Sorry! I don't understand. Speak slowly!
Linto: You speak fast.
Lifri: Sorry. Do you understand now?
Mentu: Yes, I understand. Thanks!
Linto: I have a question. What time is it?
Mentu: I don't know.
Lifri: Seven o'clock.

items.free_content_front: Lesson 9: Yesterday and Tomorrow — ca le prulamdei
items.free_content_back:
#### New words
{pu}, {ba}, {ku'i}, {cu}, {cabdei}, {bavlamdei}, {prulamdei}

#### Grammar
`pu` = past, `ba` = future, before the predicate. `cu` separates a long subject from the predicate. `.i ku'i` = but. `cabdei` today, `prulamdei` yesterday, `bavlamdei` tomorrow.

items.free_content_back: Did you go to the park?

Lifri(F): .i xu do pu klama le panka ca le prulamdei
~ Did you go to the park yesterday?
Mentu(M): go'i .i mi pu klama
~ Yes, I went.
Linto(F): .i ca le bavlamdei mi ba klama le zdani
~ Tomorrow I'll go home.

~ But today I'm here.
Lifri(F): .i le panka cu melbi
~ The park is beautiful.
Mentu(M): go'i
~ Yes!

`.au` = I wish; `.ai` = I'm going to (intent). `lo` = some/a (any), `le` = the specific one.

items.free_content_back:

#### Grammar
`pei` again: after an order it means "and you?". Chain orders: `.ai mi citka lo stasu .i .ai mi pinxe lo jisra`.

Linto(F): go'i .i .ai mi citka lo titnanba .e lo nanba
~ Yes! I'll have cookies and bread.
Mentu(M): .i le cidja cu kukte

items.free_content_front: Lesson 12: How Much? Is It Expensive? — xu ri kargu
items.free_content_back:
#### New words
{kargu}, {tolkargu}, {meryru'u}, se jdima, {pleji}, te vecnu

#### Grammar
`tol-` reverses: `kargu` expensive -> `tolkargu` cheap. Prices: `se jdima lo meryru'u be li N` = costs N dollars. `te vecnu` = buy, `pleji` = pay.

items.free_content_front: lo nanba cu se jdima lo meryru'u be li paci

# xu ri kargu
Mentu(M): .i xu lo stasu cu kargu
~ Is the soup expensive?
Lifri(F): .i lo nanba cu se jdima lo meryru'u be li paci
~ The bread costs 13 dollars.
Linto(F): .ue .i ri kargu
~ Wow, that's expensive!
Lifri(F): .i lo stasu cu se jdima lo meryru'u be li reno
~ The soup costs 20.
Mentu(M): .i xu do ponse lo jdini
~ Do you have money?
Linto(F): .i mi ba pleji
~ I'll pay.
Mentu(M): ki'e
~ Thanks!
items.free_content_back:
How Much? Is It Expensive?.
Mentu: Is the soup expensive?
Lifri: The bread costs 13 dollars.
Linto: Wow, that's expensive!
Lifri: The soup costs 20.
Mentu: Do you have money?
Linto: I'll pay.
Mentu: Thanks!

#### New words
{zarci}, {.e}, {mutce}, {drata}

#### Grammar
`.e` joins nouns: `lo titnanba .e lo jisra` = cookies and juice. `mutce` intensifies: `mutce kargu` = very expensive.

items.free_content_front: Lesson 14: Planning the Week — ca ro jeftu
items.free_content_back:
#### New words
{birti}, {jeftu}, {djedi}, {ro}, {detma'i}

#### Grammar
`ro` = every: `ca ro jeftu` = every week, `ca ro detma'i` = every month. `lo jeftu be li pa` = a one-week period. `mi birti` = I'm sure.

items.free_content_front: ca le cabdei mi zvati le zdani
ca le bavlamdei mi ba klama le panka
items.free_content_back: Tomorrow I'll go to the park.

items.free_content_front:
# ca ro jeftu
Lifri(F): .i xu mi'o penmi ca ro jeftu
~ Shall we meet every week?
Mentu(M): go'i .i mi birti
~ Yes, I'm sure.
Linto(F): .i ca le cabdei mi zvati le zdani
~ Today I'm at home.
Linto(F): .i ku'i ca le bavlamdei mi ba klama le panka
~ But tomorrow I'll go to the park.
Lifri(F): .i xu do birti
~ Are you sure?
Linto(F): go'i .i mi birti
